Creatine can help with strength and high-intensity exercise, but whether it’s appropriate for you depends on your health and medications. For most healthy adults, the usual option is creatine monohydrate, 3–5 g once daily. A loading phase—about 20 g/day split into four 5 g doses for 5–7 days—is optional, not necessary, and may cause stomach upset or temporary water-weight gain. Take it consistently; timing matters less than regular use.

Check with a clinician first if you have kidney disease, are pregnant or breastfeeding, are under 18, or take medicines that may affect kidney function. Choose a reputable, third-party-tested product and stop if you develop concerning symptoms. I don’t have enough health or medication information to say whether it’s personally safe for you.
